title: Finite coefficient actions on scalar cokernels
statement: For any integral coefficient module sheaf M, any positive level n+1, any pro-etale object U and coefficient section a on U, use [def-per-integral-lisse-reduction-data]. If a reduces to zero modulo varpi^(n+1), it acts by zero on every section of the actual scalar cokernel of M at this level. Consequently its action descends through coefficient reduction to the finite coefficient ring; restriction of that descended action recovers the original scalar cokernel.

proof.text: The uniformizer power annihilates the actual scalar cokernel: precompose its scalar endomorphism with the epic cokernel projection and apply scalar naturality and the cokernel equation. Sectionwise exactness of coefficient reduction expresses a kernel section as the uniformizer power times a continuous integral section. The module associativity law now makes its action zero. To construct the finite action, lift each finite scalar through the sectionwise surjective coefficient map. Two lifts differ by a kernel element, so their actions agree; transport the module axioms along surjectivity. Keep the original section groups and restriction maps. The latter are linear by lifting the scalar before applying their original linearity. The identity on sections identifies scalar restriction with the original module. Surjectivity likewise makes every integral-linear map between finite modules finite-linear, giving full faithfulness.
